ukmt-jmc-2012-01.title: Build it digit by digit
ukmt-jmc-2012-01.body:
Use the smallest possible digits. The thousands digit cannot be 0, so it is 1. Then the hundreds digit is 0, the tens digit is 2 and the units digit is 3, giving 1023.

**Answer: (E) 1023**

ukmt-jmc-2012-01.title: Check the options
ukmt-jmc-2012-01.body:
Only 1032, 1234 and 1023 have four different digits (1021 and 2012 repeat a digit). The smallest of these is 1023, and the construction above shows it cannot be beaten.

**Answer: (E) 1023**

ukmt-jmc-2012-02.title: Divide by 2
ukmt-jmc-2012-02.body:
$1.01\div2=0.505$ (half of 1 is 0.5 and half of 0.01 is 0.005).

**Answer: (C) 0.505**

ukmt-jmc-2012-03.title: List the factors
ukmt-jmc-2012-03.body:
6: 1, 2, 3, 6 (two others). 8: 1, 2, 4, 8 (two others). 13 and 19 are prime (none others). 25: 1, 5, 25, so exactly one other factor, 5.

**Answer: (E) 25**

ukmt-jmc-2012-04.title: Axes of symmetry
ukmt-jmc-2012-04.body:
A reflected letter can look unchanged only if the letter has a line of symmetry. U, I and O have lines of symmetry, but J, N and R do not. So 3 letters never look the same.

**Answer: (C) 3**

ukmt-jmc-2012-06.title: Rule out letters
ukmt-jmc-2012-06.body:
Faces that appear together in a view are adjacent, not opposite. From the left cube K is not opposite I or M; from the middle cube K is not opposite O or U. So K is opposite P. Neither K nor P is opposite U, and O is adjacent to U (middle cube). So U is opposite I or M. If U were opposite I, then O would be opposite M; but the right cube shows O and M (the sideways letter) on adjacent faces. So U is opposite M.

**Answer: (D) M**

ukmt-jmc-2012-07.title: Step by step
ukmt-jmc-2012-07.body:
Three small: $3\times600=1800$ pages $=$ two medium, so a medium is 900 pages. Three medium: $2700$ pages $=$ two large, so a large is 1350 pages.

**Answer: (B) 1350**

ukmt-jmc-2012-08.title: Quarters
ukmt-jmc-2012-08.body:
One quarter empty means three quarters full, so 480 ml is $\frac34$ of the tankard. One quarter is $480\div3=160$ ml.

**Answer: (B) 160 ml**

ukmt-jmc-2012-09.title: Who sees two people?
ukmt-jmc-2012-09.body:
Only Caz can see two others; everyone else sees one person or none. The person at $P$ is the only one in the picture who can see two of the others, so Caz is at $P$.

**Answer: (C) Caz**

ukmt-jmc-2012-10.title: Draw one on the other
ukmt-jmc-2012-10.body:
Drawing the arrows on the same grid, the overlap covers 4 whole $1\text{ cm}\times1\text{ cm}$ squares and 4 half squares. Area $=4+4\times\frac12=6\text{ cm}^2$.

**Answer: (E) 6 cm²**

ukmt-jmc-2012-11.title: Positive and negative parts
ukmt-jmc-2012-11.body:
Let $x$ be the sum of the added numbers and $y$ the sum of the subtracted numbers (all positive), with $123$ added. $x-y=100$ and $x+y=123+45+67+89=324$, so $x=212$, $y=112$. Since $45+67=112$, the expression is $123-45-67+89=100$ ($123+89=212$). So one $+$ and two $-$: $p-m=1-2=-1$.

**Answer: (B) $-1$**

ukmt-jmc-2012-11.title: Reduce from the all-plus total
ukmt-jmc-2012-11.body:
With all plus signs the total is $123+45+67+89=324$. Turning a $+$ into a $-$ lowers the total by twice that number, so we must lower it by $224$, i.e. the subtracted numbers add to $112$. Only $45+67=112$ works. So the expression is $123-45-67+89=100$: one plus and two minus signs, $p-m=1-2=-1$.

**Answer: (B) $-1$**

ukmt-jmc-2012-12.title: Lower bound and construction
ukmt-jmc-2012-12.body:
In a $3\times3$ square no piece can be longer than 3 squares in a row or column. In the L shape, the end square of the vertical arm, the corner square and the end square of the horizontal arm must be in three different pieces, so at least 3 pieces. Three pieces suffice: cut off the top 3 squares of the vertical arm, the last 2 squares of the horizontal arm, and keep the remaining 4 squares (an L-tetromino). Put the 3-piece along the top row of the square, the L-tetromino below it (down the left and along the bottom) and the 2-piece in the remaining middle space.

**Answer: (B) 3**

ukmt-jmc-2012-13.title: Find the factors
ukmt-jmc-2012-13.body:
Let the top factors be $p,q,r,s,t$ and the side factors $v,w,x,y,z$. From the table, $wp=15$ and $xp=18$, so $p$ divides $\gcd(15,18)=3$: $p=1$ or $3$. If $p=1$ then $w=15$, but $wr=40$ is impossible, so $p=3$, $w=5$, $x=6$. Then $r=40\div5=8$, $z=56\div8=7$, $s=60\div6=10$, $v=20\div10=2$, $q=10\div2=5$, $y=20\div5=4$, $t=24\div4=6$.

Then $A=vp=6$, $B=wq=25$, $C=xr=48$, $D=ys=40$, $E=zt=42$. Sum $=161$.

**Answer: (C) 161**

ukmt-jmc-2012-14.title: Use the period
ukmt-jmc-2012-14.body:
The pattern repeats every 6 symbols and $96=16\times6$, so symbols 97 to 102 are the same as symbols 1 to 6: ♥ ♣ ♥ ♦ ♥ ♠. The 100th and 101st are the 4th and 5th: ♦ ♥.

**Answer: (A) ♦ ♥**

ukmt-jmc-2012-15.title: Count each colour
ukmt-jmc-2012-15.body:
Yellow: 30. Not yellow: 30, of which a third (10) are red, leaving 20. A quarter of 20 (5) are pink, leaving 15 white. $\frac{15}{60}=\frac14$.

**Answer: (E) $\frac14$**

ukmt-jmc-2012-15.title: Multiply fractions
ukmt-jmc-2012-15.body:
White is what remains after taking away halves, thirds, quarters: $\left(1-\frac12\right)\!\cdot\!\left(1-\frac13\right)\!\cdot\!\left(1-\frac14\right)=\frac12\cdot\frac23\cdot\frac34=\frac14$.

**Answer: (E) $\frac14$**

ukmt-jmc-2012-16.title: Compare the two rotas
ukmt-jmc-2012-16.body:
Usually Carolyn reads pages $2,5,8,\dots$ (remainder 2 on division by 3) and George reads $3,6,9,\dots$. With Beth away Carolyn reads the odd pages and George the even pages. Carolyn reads the same pages both ways when the page is odd and $\equiv2\pmod3$: 5, 11, 17. George: multiples of 3 that are even: 6, 12, 18. Beth's pages (1, 4, 7, ...) are never the same. Total 6 pages.

**Answer: (D) 6**

ukmt-jmc-2012-17.title: Remove the extra girls
ukmt-jmc-2012-17.body:
Take away 6 girls: 18 pupils remain, equal numbers of girls and boys, 9 each. So there are 15 girls and 9 boys: $5:3$.

**Answer: (A) 5:3**

ukmt-jmc-2012-18.title: Add the row and the column
ukmt-jmc-2012-18.body:
Adding the row and column totals gives $21+21=42$. This counts each number once except $x$, which is counted twice, so $42=(2+3+4+5+6+7+8)+x=35+x$ and $x=7$.

**Answer: (D) 7**

ukmt-jmc-2012-19.title: Right-angled triangle
ukmt-jmc-2012-19.body:
In triangle $PQS$ the angle at $P$ is $90^\circ$, so $\angle PSQ+\angle PQS=90^\circ$ in ratio $1:5$: $\angle PQS=\frac56\times90^\circ=75^\circ$. Since $PQ\parallel SR$, $\angle QSR$ and $\angle PQS$ are alternate angles, so $\angle QSR=75^\circ$.

**Answer: (E) $75^\circ$**

ukmt-jmc-2012-20.title: Convert to years and months
ukmt-jmc-2012-20.body:
50 months $=4$ years 2 months; 50 weeks is about $11\frac12$ months (a year is 52 weeks); 50 days is about $1\frac23$ months. Total about $54$ years $+\,(2+11\frac12+1\frac23)$ months $=54$ years $+\,15\frac16$ months $=55$ years $3\frac16$ months. So his next birthday is his 56th.

**Answer: (A) 56**

ukmt-jmc-2012-21.title: Dominoes as edges
ukmt-jmc-2012-21.body:
Call the dominoes (1,2), (1,5), (2,5), (4,5), (4,6), (5,6). A ring means a closed chain in which adjacent dominoes share a number. The numbers 1, 2 and 4 each appear on exactly two dominoes, which must therefore be adjacent: (1,2)-(1,5), (1,2)-(2,5) and (4,5)-(4,6), (4,6)-(5,6) are forced. So the chain (1,5),(1,2),(2,5) and the chain (4,5),(4,6),(5,6) are joined end to end through 5s. The domino (1,5) is an end of its chain, so it touches (1,2) and one of (4,5), (5,6). It can never touch (2,5) or (4,6). That is 2 dominoes.

**Answer: (B) 2**

ukmt-jmc-2012-22.title: Small triangles
ukmt-jmc-2012-22.body:
Drawing in the extra lines divides the hexagon into 54 small congruent equilateral triangles, of which 12 are shaded: $\frac{12}{54}=\frac29$.

**Answer: (B) $\frac29$**

ukmt-jmc-2012-22.title: Six big triangles
ukmt-jmc-2012-22.body:
The hexagon is 6 congruent equilateral triangles, each made of 9 small triangles, of which 2 are shaded. So $\frac29$ of the hexagon is shaded.

**Answer: (B) $\frac29$**

ukmt-jmc-2012-23.title: Check the possible changes
ukmt-jmc-2012-23.body:
Changing the hundreds or tens digit leaves the units digit 0, so the number is a multiple of 10 and not prime. Changing the units digit gives 201 to 209: 202, 204, 206, 208 are even, 205 is a multiple of 5, $201=3\times67$, $203=7\times29$, $207=9\times23$, $209=11\times19$. None is prime.

**Answer: (A) 0**

ukmt-jmc-2012-24.title: Wins and losses
ukmt-jmc-2012-24.body:
I have won $0.49\times500=245$ games and lost $255$. To reach 50% I need as many wins as losses; the losses stay at 255, so I need $255-245=10$ more wins, i.e. 10 more games.

**Answer: (D) 10**

ukmt-jmc-2012-25.title: Diophantine equation
ukmt-jmc-2012-25.body:
The angles sum to $180$: $8x+13y+50=180$, so $8x+13y=130$, i.e. $8x=13(10-y)$. As 8 and 13 are coprime, $13\mid x$; write $x=13a$, giving $8a=10-y$. With $y$ positive, $10-y\in\{1,\dots,9\}$ and a multiple of 8, so $10-y=8$, $y=2$, $a=1$, $x=13$. Then $x+y=15$.

**Answer: (A) 15**

ukmt-jmc-2012-25.title: Check by trying $y$
ukmt-jmc-2012-25.body:
$8x=130-13y$ must be a positive multiple of 8. Trying $y=1,\dots,9$: $130-13y=117,104,91,78,65,52,39,26,13$; only $104$ is divisible by 8 ($x=13$, $y=2$). So $x+y=15$.

**Answer: (A) 15**
